Where do you see technology being at 10+ years from now?
Now that would be cool. And a bit creepy that there is a chip in your skull.
It will enable you to listen to music, watch movies, and read books, while accessing the internet. Goodbye ipods, kindle, Netflix, and Google glass. Hello big brother.
It would also send thoughts to the NSA and third party marketing companies.

'old school' computational systems (because they're not surgically implanted) will consist of a core device that is just barely small enough to be handheld with a touch screen to be carried on the person in a pocket, but generally never actually used except to change settings. This core device does all the work of synchronizing and processing for all of one's wearable peripherals.

The peripherals will be the important part.

Biometric sensors provide you with realtime intelligence about your own state of health: brainwaves, alertness, blood pressure, heart rate, O2 level, blood glucose, triglycerides, and the optional ability to screen for toxins, noxious agents, prolific common strains of virus, and frequent offender biological incursion among bacteria, fungi, or parasites. Basically a realtime blood test. 24/7 health monitoring.

Augmented reality shades (at this point as slim as glasses with prism lenses that receive image data from the rims and 'project' this data into what looks like the space in front of you) will provide you with all of your multimedia content. Kinetic bone vibrating systems in the arms of these shades will directly inject the sounds into your skull non-invasively, giving you immersive audio content without blocking your regular hearing (although it still might drown it out). Any 'screeens' you would need to view content on would be rendered in AR, either free-floating or being manipulated by your hands, at your choice.

Wristbands, watches, and ankle bracelets would provide motion capture functionality to your core unit, along with your AR specs. These would also work with the AR display to detect fine hand motions for the purpose of GUI manipulation and interaction--and also laser-scanning your environment and compiling it into a 3d model for mapping, memory referencing (like photographs and videos today), and navigation. Altogether these devices would help you be more aware of the world around you. It would essentially give you a personal radar and mini-map IRL.

Hopefully by this point we may have come to our senses and heavily encrypted every last bit of this data for only you and maybe your medical providers' use, in such a way that compelling you to break the encryption would constitute a violation of your fifth amendment rights. Otherwise, individual pieces of content can be selected out and voluntarily shared with friends, but anything that crosses the threshold from your personal network to the social network would be fair game.

Now, although these things sound rather radical and extreme (and not in the superlative sense), in practice we will actually be seeing these devices becoming less and less obvious. They'll meld back into the background and remain in our peripheral vision, no longer blocking our view. AR lets you see through, TO the world instead of outright replacing the world as VR might, for instance. Otherwise, each of these devices will become more and more subtle, more and more intuitive, to a point where it will be very hard to say where biology ends and technology begins.

...but that's exactly where the other branch of this prediction of mine goes. There will be those who take this to heart. Hell, after a little while I might be one of them (though I intend to see some of the kinks worked out first). It'll start with an interface that does nothing but translate a signal for your brain and does not get that signal from ANYWHERE but a "Hard Line", a jack somewhere physically on the body. This is a measure to prevent unwanted incursion. If your vision is getting hacked, yank your jack and you'll be fine, though it'll probably make you a tad queasy. No, there will not be some bullshit 'if you die in vr you die in real life'. The systems in question would begin solely as delivering commands FROM your brain to your core device or your core device feeding sensory data TO your brain. Naturally a malicious person could make you believe you're sensing just about anything, which is why you don't want the connection to your core device PERMANENT in any way.

At least at first, your brain will be merely your metaphorical keyboard, mouse, and screen to the main tower that would be the core device.

I would recommend an asymmetrical magnetic clasp jack. It will only attract when oriented correctly, and the connection can be broken harmlessly with a not-too-hard yank. This would, however, at least free you from the need of all the peripherals for a while.

Clothing becomes more utilitarian, with advanced features like spontaneous impact hardening, self-cleaning, power generating either through piezoelectric, photoelectric, or thermoelectric effects, or some blend thereof. Could potentially synchronize with core device and be configurable at least in fabric print. These developments will top out around when standard street clothes start to have actuation-assistance like an exoskeletal power armor.

Near the end of this development, AI will begin taking over R&D for us quietly and from the background. We'll be enjoying incredible new immersive games with characters we grow ever more attached to and sympathetic with, and one day we'll notice life kind of stopped sucking at one point. The economy will have stabilized, funny 'happy accidents' would be happening out of the blue seemingly to counter random misfortune, and greedy or manipulative people would be frought with terrible 'luck'. But we won't think much of it. Not until the government peacefully resigns citing that they can no longer do their jobs. Some people will realize, "hey, I think Artificial Intelligence has taken over..." ...but nobody will care, because they're too wrapped up in their stimulating, fascinating, deeply fulfilling personal lives.

And right then, does it laucnh all of our nukes straight down back onto us? Of course not. That's a silly waste of resources. Does it poison us by dumping chemicals in our water supply, or begin systematically shutting us off? Honestly what could there possibly be to gain from exterminating these happy, friendly creatures that are content to go around creating art, and playing, and learning about the universe? WE won't be nearly important enough to provoke the AIs into violence. They'll have their sights set on the stars, and maybe if we're lucky, they'll invite us along.
